question: Which of the following documents is referred to as the 'Magna Carta of the Indian people'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Queen's Proclamation of 1858**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Queen's Proclamation of 1858, also known as the "Proclamation by the Queen in Council," marked the formal transfer of power from the East India Company to the British Crown.
 
• It is referred to as the "Magna Carta of the Indian people" because it promised equal treatment of Indian subjects and British citizens under the law.
 
• The proclamation assured non-interference in religious practices and customs, which was a significant step toward addressing Indian grievances post the Revolt of 1857.
 
• Queen Victoria declared that Indians would be eligible for government positions based on their education and ability, promoting a sense of fairness.
 
• The proclamation was issued on November 1, 1858, and was read by Lord Canning, the first Viceroy of India, in Allahabad.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revolt of 1857:**

 
 
• Also known as the First War of Independence, it was a widespread but unsuccessful rebellion against British rule in India.
 
• The revolt was triggered by grievances related to social, economic, and political issues, including the introduction of the Enfield rifle cartridges rumored to be greased with cow and pig fat.
 
 
 
• **Indian Councils Act of 1861:**
 
 
• This act marked the beginning of legislative reforms in India under British rule.
 
• It introduced the concept of non-official Indian members in the legislative council.
 
 
 
• **Charter Act of 1833:**
 
 
• This act centralized administrative power by making the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India.
 
• It opened up civil services to Indians, though the provision was rarely implemented.
 
 
 
• **Treaty of Allahabad (1765):**
 
 
• Signed between the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II and Robert Clive, this treaty granted the East India Company Diwani rights (revenue collection) in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.
 
• It marked the beginning of British political control in India.
